take_homes: Don't split into several agents by default. Split only when they need different access, speak a different dialect or must disagree. Otherwise use one good prompt.

The places where work is handed from one agent to another are where it goes wrong. The agent-to-agent review checks those handoffs, not whether the final answer is true, so a person still has to question it.
Moving a risky step from 'do' to 'propose' keeps a human in the loop. That is something I can bring to my leadership team.

misconception.why: The module was about how to build agent systems and never about roles or headcount. The only people-related moments, the access boundary and 'propose' over 'do', made me think about oversight. They did not change my belief about which roles go first.

one_line: Good on when not to build several agents, and honest that you can't yet trust the answer. It never said what this means for the people who currently do this work.
